summary.en: Joseph Kabila, the former president, has joined rebel forces and is coordinating attacks with the M23 movement against the Congolese government. Rwanda's defence ministry and its military bank Zigama have been sanctioned for supplying M23 and facilitating a gold-smuggling route that funds an Islamic State-linked insurgency in eastern DRC. The FRN reported the capture of several positions in Rugezi after a week of fighting, while two army generals and over 600 soldiers defected to Kabila-led rebels. The conflict caused 1,158 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Joseph Kabila, den tidligere presidenten, har sluttet seg til opprørsstyrker og koordinerer angrep med M23-bevegelsen mot den kongoske regjeringen. Rwandas forsvarsdepartement og militærbanken Zigama har blitt sanksjonert for å levere til M23 og legge til rette for en gullsmuglingsrute som finansierer en IS-tilknyttet opprør i Øst-DRC. FRN rapporterte at de erobret flere posisjoner i Rugezi etter en ukes kamper, mens to hærgeneraler og over 600 soldater gikk over til Kabila-ledede opprørere. Konflikten forårsaket 1 158 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: M23 campaign (2022–present)
background.extract: The M23 campaign is an ongoing series of military offensives launched by the March 23 Movement (M23), a Rwandan-backed rebel paramilitary group in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, since March 2022. In November 2021, M23 first launched attacks against the Congolese military (FARDC) and MONUSCO, seizing military positions in Ndiza, Cyanzu, and Runyoni in North Kivu Province. This coincided with the deployment of Uganda People's Defence Force (UPDF) to the region to combat the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a Ugandan rebel group operating in the Congo's North Kivu and Ituri provinces.
